title: Ferrero Rocher Chocolate Cookies
description: Sometimes you crave something truly rich, indulgent, and super chocolatey. That’s exactly what these Ferrero Rocher cookies are. Chocolate dough wrapped around a crunchy candy, with melted Nutella surrounding it. The result is a gooey cookie with a liquid hazelnut-chocolate center.
steps: In a mixer bowl, beat room-temperature butter with the paddle attachment on medium speed for about 2 minutes.
Add the sugar and beat for another 2–3 minutes, until the mixture is light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed until combined.
Add all dry ingredients (cocoa, flour, starch, baking soda, salt) and mix until fully combined.
Add chocolate chips and chopped hazelnuts, mix on low speed to incorporate.
Divide the dough into balls, about 100 g each.
Make an indentation in each ball, forming something like a “nest.”
Dip a Ferrero Rocher candy into Nutella. Place it in the center of the “nest” and carefully wrap the dough around it so it is completely covered.
Place the shaped dough balls in the refrigerator for 3–4 hours.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (~350°F).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the dough balls at least 2 cm (~1 in) apart.
Bake for 20–25 minutes.
The baked cookies can be stored for 5–7 days in an airtight container at room temperature.
Raw dough balls can be frozen for up to 3 months. Before baking, place them directly on a baking sheet and bake slightly longer without thawing.

title: BLUEBERRY-LEMON ROLLS RECIPE
description: My recent obsession—the floral notes of blueberry paired with the explosive tang of lemon. The combination of the aroma of a fresh buttery bun with the scent of lemon zest and the delicate fragrance of blueberries is going to make your head spin!

ingredients.name: strong flour (I use Zernari Select, bread flour will work)
soft unsalted butter
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: lemon zest
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

steps: Mix warm milk, sugar, butter, and yeast. Add the egg, yolk, zest, and salt. Stir in the flour and knead into a soft, sticky dough — cover and let rise in a warm place (~1–2 hours).
Place the blueberries in a saucepan over medium heat. Add sugar and lemon pieces. Dissolve the starch in the juice and pour into the mixture. Stirring constantly, cook until it comes to a boil.
For the curd, place all ingredients in a saucepan, combine thoroughly, and while stirring bring to a boil. Strain through a sieve.
For the bottom icing layer, combine the butter with zest. Grease the bottom of the pan with it(~35–40 × 25–30 cm).
For the spread, combine the butter with sugar, salt, juice, and zest.
Roll out the dough into a thin rectangle and evenly spread the butter mixture over it. Add the blueberry filling (set aside 20 g).
Roll into a log, cut into 8 pieces, and place in a baking dish. Let rise for another ~1 hour. Bake at 175°C (~350°F) for 25–30 minutes.

Whip cream cheese with the heavy whipping cream and remaining blueberry filling. Spread over the still-warm buns, make an indentation in the center, and place 1–2 tbsp of lemon curd inside. Decorate with blueberries.

title: MANDARIN-PASSIONFRUIT CUPCAKES
description: These aren’t just cupcakes — they’re a firework of flavor! A celebration, unforgettable bliss, and an endorphin injection all in a single bite I created this recipe for the Winter holiday season, but didn’t post it in time, and keeping it a secret any longer feels like a crime. If you can’t find mandarins, grab some oranges and start baking now
steps: Place softened butter, oil, and sugar in the mixer bowl. Beat for about 5 min., until the mixture becomes pale and fluffy
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla
Sift and combine dry ingredients
Reduce mixer speed and add half of the dry ingredients
Add kefir, mix thoroughly
Add the remaining dry ingredients and combine
Distribute batter into cupcake liners, filling them about 2/3 full. Bake in a preheated oven at 170–180°C (~340–355°F) for 20–25 min
Pour purée into a saucepan and add mandarin pulp (1). Place over heat
Mix sugar with pectin and gradually sprinkle it into the saucepan while stirring
Mix gelatin in cold water and let it bloom
Bring the mixture to a boil, then remove from the heat. Add gelatin and stir until fully dissolved
Fold in mandarin pulp (2), cover the filling with food wrap, ensure it touches the entire surface, and refrigerate until set
Bring purée to a boil and pour it over finely chopped (or callets) white chocolate and cocoa butter. Let it sit for 1 minute, and mix until smooth
Add cream, stir, cover with food wrap, ensure it touches the entire surface, and refrigerate overnight
Add mascarpone and whip until frosting reaches a stable consistency
Scoop out the center of cupcakes, soak with 2–3 tsp of Cointreau, add filling, frost, and decorate. You can use rum instead of Cointreau

title: RECIPE: PUMPKIN CREAM SOUP
description: Pumpkin cream soup with lentils is all about warmth, comfort, balanced flavor — and nourishment. Its velvety texture, the gentle sweetness of butternut squash, hearty lentils, and aromatic spices make this soup perfect for cold days. Turkey adds protein and depth of flavor, while cream gives the soup a rich, silky consistency. For 2.0–3.0 L of water:

ingredients.name: pork fat for cracklings (optional) or 2 tbsp oil
Spices to taste (black pepper, smoked paprika, turmeric or curry, nutmeg)

steps: Bring 2–3 L of water to a boil. Add the turkey thigh, chopped pumpkin and carrot, and 300–400 g of rinsed lentils. Simmer over low heat for 30–40 minutes.
In a frying pan, lightly fry the diced pork fat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook, stirring, until golden.
(If not using pork fat, sauté the onion in 2 tbsp of oil.)
Season with salt, pepper, paprika, turmeric, and nutmeg to taste. Pour in the cream or add the cream cheese, bring to a gentle boil, then remove from heat.
Remove the turkey thigh and cut the meat into small pieces. Blend the soup until smooth. Return the turkey pieces to the soup.
Serve topped with onion cracklings and pumpkin seeds.
Optionally, add croutons or shredded braised meat (veal).

title: RECIPE: PUMPKIN MARBLE LOAF CAKE
description: An ideal dessert for the colder season, combining the gentle sweetness of spiced pumpkin with the warming richness of chocolate. A simple recipe that creates a cozy, comforting atmosphere
steps: Chocolate batter:
Preheat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Line a loaf pan (~23 × 10 cm) with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the sugar, melted butter, pumpkin purée, milk, and eggs.
In a separate bowl, whisk together all the dry ingredients: flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and spices.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and mix until smooth and fully combined.
In a separate bowl, mix ⅓ of the pumpkin batter with the cocoa powder and milk until smooth.
Spoon the batters into the pan, alternating layers of pumpkin and chocolate batter. Gently tap the pan to evenly distribute the batter.
Bake at 180°C for about 70–80 minutes, until risen and golden. Check for doneness with a skewer.
Let the cake cool in the pan for 10–15 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
P.S. To achieve a thick pumpkin purée, roast the pumpkin in small pieces at 180°C (356°F) with convection for about 45–60 minutes.

title: Tart Cherry-Coconut Swirls
description: Who else loves baking with tart cherries as much as I do?—Today is your day! These soft, fluffy, feather-light sweet swirls with crunchy coconut flakes and the juicy tartness of ripe cherries just melt in your mouth, delivering incredible pleasure!

ingredients.name: strong flour (I use Zernari Select, any bread flour will work)
soft unsalted butter
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: coconut flakes
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream 33–36% or coconut cream 12–18%

steps: Mix warm milk, sugar, butter, and yeast. Add egg, yolk, and salt. Gradually mix in the flour, then knead into a soft, sticky dough—cover and let rise in a warm place (~1–2 hours).
Place tart cherries in a saucepan over medium heat. Add sugar. Dissolve the cornstarch in the lemon juice, then stir it into the mixture. Cook, stirring, until it boils.
For the bottom layer icing (optional), mix soft butter with sugar, salt, and coconut flakes. Spread on the bottom of a pan (~35–40 × 25–30 cm).
For the spread, grind the coconut flakes in a coffee grinder into a paste. Mix butter with sugar, salt, and coconut paste.
Roll out the dough into a thin rectangular sheet and evenly spread the spread over it. Add 1/2 of the cherry filling.
Roll into a log, cut into 8 pieces, and place into a baking dish. Let it rise again for another hour. Bake at 175°C  (~350°F) for 25–30 minutes.

Whip cream cheese or mascarpone with heavy cream and coconut flakes. Spread the icing on warm swirls, forming a slight indentation in the center, and place 1 tbsp of cherry filling in it. Sprinkle with coconut flakes.

title: Caramel Apple Cinnamon Rolls
description: The aroma of caramel, apples, cinnamon, and freshly baked dough is enough to drive anyone crazy — your hand just reaches for another roll on its own Make them and see for yourself!

ingredients.name: soft unsalted butter
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: caramel sauce (from my previous post)
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream (33–36%)
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: cinnamon
ingredients.section: Optional Bottom Layer Icing (for extra tenderness and juiciness)

ingredients.name: caramel sauce (recipe is a bit earlier on my profile)

steps: caramelized apples
+ extra caramel for drizzling
⤵ Instructions
Add sugar to a pan and set it over high heat. Once the sugar has melted, add the soft butter and stir until combined.
Add the apples and cinnamon. Cook over high heat for a few minutes, stirring constantly, until the apples turn slightly translucent and excess liquid evaporates. Remove from heat and cool.
Mix the warm milk, sugar, butter, and yeast. Add the egg, yolk, and salt. Fold in the sifted flour and knead into a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise (~1–2 hours). Then roll it out thinly and spread the filling evenly on top. Add caramel and apples.
Roll into a log, cut into 8 pieces, and place into a baking dish (spread the bottom layer icing first).
Let it rise for another hour. Bake at 175°C (~350°F) for 25–35 minutes.
Combine room-temperature cream cheese or mascarpone with slightly warm caramel. Add the whipping cream and whip. Spread over warm rolls and drizzle with caramel.
P.S. For the filling and bottom layer icing, mix all ingredients together by hand with a spatula or using a stand mixer with a paddle attachment.

title: Chocolate Cinnamon Rolls with Baileys Recipe
description: You loved the previous Cinnamon Roll recipes so much that I’m considering creating a separate PDF collection. What do you think? This time, a more restrained, “adult” flavor — chocolate with your favorite Baileys liqueur, which I’m sure will make everyone fall in love from the very first bite of this soft, juicy, and aromatic bun

ingredients.name: strong flour (I use Zernari Select,  bread flour works too)

steps: cocoa for sprinkling
Mix together milk, sugar, melted butter, and yeast. Add the egg, yolk, and salt. Stir in the flour sifted with cocoa and knead a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise (~1–2 h, depending on the room temp). Then roll it out thinly and spread the chocolate filling evenly.
Roll it up, cut into 8 pieces, and place in a baking dish (spread the bottom layer icing first).
Let it rise again for 1 hour. Bake at 175 °C (~350°F) for 30–35 minutes.
Beat the well-chilled mascarpone with Baileys. Spread on the warm Cinnamon Rolls. Drizzle some more Baileys, and sprinkle with cocoa.

title: TIRAMISU CHEESECAKE WITH BAILEYS
description: Imagine a meeting of two legends — tiramisu and cheesecake — a crispy shortcrust base, silky creamy mascarpone and Baileys filling, aromatic coffee and liqueur generously soaking the Savoiardi biscuits, and a light bitter cocoa finish.
steps: - Shortcrust dough
Combine soft butter and powdered sugar using a paddle or whisk attachment. Add almond flour and mix.
Add half the regular flour and half the eggs, mix. Add the remaining eggs and flour, gently combine.
Wrap in plastic wrap in a thin layer and chill. Bake at 175°C until golden, breaking the dough into small pieces first.
In a blender, add pieces of shortcrust dough and almond flakes, grind to fine crumbs.
Add chopped hazelnuts, sugar, and melted butter. Mix thoroughly.
Line the bottom of a ring mold with foil and the sides with acetate sheet, then press the base mixture tightly.
Place mascarpone, sugar, Baileys, and vanilla extract in a mixer bowl and gently mix until smooth.
Add cream and whisk to thick consistency (or whip separately and fold in gently).
Spread half the cheese mixture over the base. Soak Savoiardi in coffee and liqueur and place the biscuit layer.
Spread the remaining cheese mixture on top, smooth evenly, and refrigerate overnight to set.
Decorate with whipped cream and cocoa.

title: Mega-Chocolate Cinnamon Rolls Recipe
description: …baked them over the weekend — the kids devoured two batches in one evening! …made the cinnamon rolls again today — they’re divine — so delicious and fluffy like a feather! …I’m not even thinking what to make for the birthday anymore, who needs cake — there’ll be cinnamon rolls When we made them for the first time, we couldn’t even tell — is it dough with some chocolate or chocolate with just a little bit of dough? Fluffy dough, chocolate filling with cinnamon, chocolate chips, and fragrant orange peel. All this wrapped in a hug of chocolate icing

ingredients.name: strong flour (I use Zernari Select, bread flour works too)
candied orange peel (recipe on my profile, check the Reels tab)

steps: cocoa powder for dusting
Mix together milk, sugar, melted butter, and yeast. Add the egg, yolk, and salt. Stir in the flour sifted with cocoa and knead a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise (~1–2 h). Then roll it out thinly and spread the chocolate filling evenly. Add chocolate chips and candied peel.
Roll it up, cut into 8 pieces, and place in a baking dish (spread the bottom layer icing first).
Let rise again for 1–1.5 h. Bake at 175 °C for 30–35 minutes.
For the glaze, mix all ingredients together. Spread over warm rolls and dust with cocoa.

title: Caramel-Nut Cinnamon Roll Recipe
description: Soft as clouds, with a pleasant crunch of the nuts. So juicy that they melt in your mouth, leaving a divine aftertaste of nuts and salted caramel. Each bite makes you fall in love even more Imagine incredibly fluffy rolls of chocolate dough with a hint of cinnamon, soaked in caramel, filled with a nutty filling, and topped with a creamy nut frosting plus extra caramel and chopped nuts. This dessert perfectly combines the cozy charm of homemade baked goods with the beloved caramel-and-nut flavor combination

ingredients.name: nut paste/butter (I used hazelnut, but any nut paste or Nutella works)

steps: salted caramel
roasted nuts
Mix milk, sugar, butter, and yeast. Add the egg, yolk, and salt. Gradually incorporate the flour previously sifted with cocoa and knead a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise (~1 hour), then roll it out and evenly spread the nut filling. Add caramel and nuts on top.
Roll into a log, cut into 8 pieces, and place in a baking pan (pre-grease the bottom with the bottom layer).
Let it rise for another hour. Bake at 175°C (~350°F) for 25–35 minutes.
Prepare the glaze. Spread over warm Cinnamon rolls, drizzle with caramel, and sprinkle with nuts.

title: Tiramisu Cinnamon Roll Recipe
description: Light as a cloud, juicy enough to make your head spin—with every bite, they win your heart over more and more. Imagine soft, fluffy rolls with the aroma of coffee and cinnamon, filled with a chocolate-coffee filling, and topped with delicate mascarpone icing. This dessert combines the warmth of homemade baking with the elegance of classic tiramisu
steps: Cocoa for dusting
Optional bottom layer (for extra tenderness and juiciness):
Mix milk, sugar, butter, and yeast together. Add eggs, salt, and espresso. Gradually mix in flour and knead into soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise (~1 hour), then roll it out and evenly spread the coffee filling over it.
Roll into a log, cut into 8 pieces, and place in a pan (you can grease the bottom with the optional layer).
Let rise again for 1 hour. Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 25–30 minutes.
Prepare the mascarpone icing with heavy whip cream, sugar, and vanilla. Spread over the warm cinnamon roll and dust with cocoa.

title: LEMON—RASPBERRY CUPCAKES
description: While raspberries are still in season, be sure to make these tender cupcakes with a touch of lemon and juicy berries! Ingredients (12-14 pcs ~60 g each)
steps: Put the softened butter, lemon zest, and sugar in a mixer bowl. Beat for 3 min until the color lightens
Add eggs one at a time
Mix in sour cream
Sift flour, mixed with baking powder and salt. Add dry ingredients to the base and combine
Add raspberries, gently fold them in
Divide the batter into paper liners, filling them 3/4 full
Bake at 180°C (~355°F) for 20-25 min, check readiness with a toothpick
Whisk eggs with yolks until smooth
Bring lemon juice and sugar to a boil
Pour the hot juice in a thin stream into the egg mixture, whisking constantly
Transfer the mixture to a saucepan, cook over low heat, stirring constantly
Remove from the heat, and gradually add butter
Strain through a sieve, cover the surface with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight
Whip lemon curd with mascarpone until smooth
Decorate frosting and fresh raspberries

title: BANANA TEA CAKE WITH DATES AND NUTS
description: This cake is a true harmony of texture and flavor. The sweetness of bananas and dates creates a juicy base, while dark rum adds depth and subtle caramel notes. Crunchy walnuts bring balance and a lovely bite. Simple to make, yet looks and tastes like a showstopper
steps: - Lightly roast the walnuts in the oven at 170-180°C for about 5-6 minutes until light golden color and pleasant aroma. Let them cool down and coarse chop them.
- Put sugar, butter, water, rum and chopped dates
in a saucepan. Stirring occasionally, heat the mixture until sugar and butter have dissolved. Then increase the heat and bring the mixture to a boil.
- Remove the saucepan from the heat, pour the mixture into a large bowl and let it cool down to room temperature.
- if you do not want to use alcohol, you can replace it with water
- In a separate bowl, beat eggs, banana puree and
vanilla paste until fluffy. Pour into the cooled mixture, add baking soda and mix until smooth. Add chopped walnuts, and mix again.
- Combine flour, baking powder and salt, sift. Add
to the batter and mix until smooth.
- Grease the molds with butter and dust them with
some flour. Pour the batter into the molds, filling them approximately ⅔ (~ 680 g of batter per 1 tea cake).

- Bake at 180°C for 40-50 minutes. Check if the tea cakes are ready with a wooden skewer. Take the tea cakes out of the oven, let them cool down for about 5 mins and carefully remove them from of the molds. Place on a wire rack to cool down.
Basque cheesecake — a dessert with character. Its caramelized, slightly burnt crust hides a silky, creamy center that simply melts in your mouth.
The combination of cream cheese, heavy cream, and vanilla creates an incredible tenderness, like softened ice cream, while the caramel notes of the burnt top add a special charm.

Recently, during one of my masterclasses, a student came up to me to thank me for the best Basque cheesecake recipe. Then she asked if she could share it with other students. I was surprised, since the recipe has always been available to everyone.
She then showed me a photo of a notebook page written in my handwriting with this very recipe.
It turned out that five years ago, during a class, I had shared this new recipe with my students and let them photograph a page from my notebook.

What touched me most is that the notebook has long been gone, yet the photo of that page is still being used today to bake this beloved cheesecake. That’s why I decided to share it once again with all of you — without hesitation, one of my very best recipes!
It’s incredibly easy and quick to make, and disappears from the plate even faster!
Don’t believe me? Save this post right now so you don’t lose it, and hurry to try it yourself!
- Line an 18 cm (h = 6–8 cm) baking ring or pan with two sheets of parchment, forming high edges.
- Place all ingredients in a blender and mix until smooth. Pour the mixture into the pan.
- Bake for ~30–35 min at 230°C, top-and-bottom mode. The cheesecake should be burnt on top but still jiggly inside.
- If the top isn’t browned enough, switch to grill mode for 2 minutes at 230–240°C.
- Let it cool, then refrigerate overnight to stabilize.

title: BANANA CUPCAKE RECIPE
description: A dessert that speaks for itself—an all-out banana explosion. Because here, banana isn't just an ingredient—it's the star of the show: soft banana cupcake with crunchy nuts and chocolate chips, combined with a juicy banana center and delicate banana frosting, all create an explosion of flavor You won’t be able to stop, I guarantee it!
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (~355°F). Prepare your cupcake pan by lining it with paper liners.
In a bowl, combine all dry ingredients: all-purpose and almond flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Sift together.
Mash the bananas into a purée. Add the sour cream, lemon juice, sugar, eggs, and oil. Mix until smooth.
Add the dry mixture to the banana base. Mix until the texture is smooth.
Fold in the nuts and chocolate chips.
Evenly distribute the batter into the liners, filling each about two-thirds full. Insert a slice of fresh banana into the center of each one before baking.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Let the cupcakes cool on a wire rack.
The whipped banana cream—the same recipe that is already on my profile (scroll back a few posts )—is the perfect complement to these incredibly delicious cupcakes.

title: Banana Whipped Ganache
description: - If you’ve been looking for a reliable and stable frosting that you also want to eat straight from the bowl with a spoon—here it is! Delicate, not overly sweet, super light, and incredibly delicious. And it comes with a rich banana flavor Banana-infused cream:
steps: Cut the very ripe bananas into pieces, pour the cream over them, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight to do the cold infusion.
Strain the banana-infused cream through a sieve. Don’t throw away the bananas—you can use them to bake a delicious banana bread.
Banana whipped ganache:
Soak the gelatin in cold water and let it bloom.

In a saucepan, bring 95 g of the banana cream (1) to until just boiling (do not boil). Pour it over the white chocolate callets, let sit for 30–40 seconds, then stir with a silicone spatula until smooth.

- You can adjust the amount of gelatin to change the firmness of the frosting to your liking. Also, it’s a good idea to adapt the gelatin amount depending on the cocoa butter content in your chocolate.
Melt the bloomed gelatin in the microwave, then pour it into the cream–chocolate mixture and mix thoroughly.
Add the remaining 105 g of banana cream (2), stir, and cover the entire surface of the ganache with plastic food wrap. Refrigerate for at least 10–12 hours to set.
Transfer the chilled ganache to a mixer bowl, add the mascarpone and vanilla paste (or seeds from a vanilla bean), and whip until it turns into a stable creamy mass.

title: MATCHA STRAWBERRY TIRAMISU
description: This is the moment when the flavor goes beyond expectations — light, refreshing, and perfectly summery. The gentle herbal bitterness of matcha and juicy, fragrant strawberries create an incredible flavor duet. - Even those who don’t usually like matcha say: “This is so delicious!” Be sure to save the recipe and don’t forget to thank me in the comments!
steps: Mix the yolks and sugar into a heatproof bowl, and set over a hot water bath.
Stir constantly with a whisk, heat to 60°C (~140°F), and hold over a water bath for another 2–3 minutes to pasteurize the yolks.
Transfer to a mixer bowl, let cool to room temperature, and beat until the yolks turn light and pale and increase in volume.
Add mascarpone and matcha; mix until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the cold heavy whipping cream to soft peaks, then gently fold into the yolk mixture with a spatula.
For the soak, combine matcha and sugar, pour over with hot water, and mix thoroughly with a milk frother or spiral whisk. Add the milk and mix again.
Spread a thin layer of frosting on the bottom of your dish. Quickly dip half (~175–200 g) of the Savoiardi biscuits in the soaking syrup and arrange as the first layer.
Evenly spread 1/4 of the frosting on top. Then add a layer of diced strawberries and cover with another 1/4 of the frosting.
Soak the remaining Savoiardi biscuits and lay out the second Tiramisu layer.
Evenly spread the remaining half of the frosting on top and generously dust with matcha through a sieve.
Chill in the fridge for at least 10–12 hours for the Tiramisu to set

title: BAILEYS TIRAMISU
description: Classic tiramisu is already truly special: soft, creamy, rich with coffee flavor. But add a touch of Baileys—and it turns into pure indulgence that’s dangerously addictive Here’s the recipe for a perfectly balanced, decadent tiramisu that will definitely earn you tons of compliments! Save it, make it—and let me know what you think of this variation!
steps: + 350–400 g Savoiardi (ladyfinger biscuits)
Mix the yolks and sugar into a heatproof bowl, and set over a hot water bath.
Stir constantly with a whisk, heat to 60°C (~140°F), and hold over a water bath for another 2–3 minutes to pasteurize the yolks.
Transfer to a mixer bowl, let cool to room temperature, and beat until the yolks turn light and pale and increase in volume.
Add mascarpone and vanilla seeds; mix until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the cold heavy whipping cream to soft peaks, then gently fold into the yolk mixture with a spatula.
For the soak, stir Baileys into the espresso.
Spread a thin layer of frosting on the bottom of your dish. Quickly dip half (~175–200 g) of the Savoiardi biscuits in the coffee mixture and arrange as the first layer.
Spoon and evenly spread half of the frosting on top of the biscuits. Soak the remaining biscuits and form the second layer.
Finish with the rest of the frosting, smooth the top, and dust generously with cocoa powder.
Chill in the fridge for at least 10–12 hours for the Tiramisu to set.

title: MANGO GANACHE
description: Love at first spoonful: delicate, vibrant, and full of flavor
steps: Bring the mango purée, heavy whipping cream, glucose syrup, and inverted sugar to a boil.
Pour the mango mixture over the white chocolate callets and cocoa butter, and emulsify using @bamix_ua immersion blender.
Cool to below 28°C (~ 83°F), and your ganache is ready to use.
Shelf life: Up to 3 weeks at 4°C.
- Tip: I recommend using high-quality white chocolate with at least 30% cocoa butter content.

title: CHOCO–PEANUT BUTTER CUPCAKES RECIPE
description: A flavor that resonates with many — chocolate, salted caramel, and peanut butter.

ingredients.name: fleur de sel or ⅓ tsp salt

steps: 2large eggs (Grade A)
Preheat the oven to 160°C (~320°F) and line a cupcake tray with paper liners (large, 60–70 g of batter each)
Boil and weigh 120 g of water; let it cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine all dry ingredients using a hand whisk
Add all wet ingredients, including the boiled water, in a separate bowl, and whisk until smooth
Slowly pour the wet mixture into the dry, gently mixing until thoroughly combined with no lumps
Fill cupcake liners about ⅔ full and bake for 20–25 minutes. Let cool in the tray for 5 minutes, then remove and cool completely on a wire rack

Place sugar, water, and glucose syrup in a saucepan and begin heating. Simultaneously bring the heavy whipping cream to a boil in a separate pot. Once the sugar syrup turns golden (~170–180°C), stirring constantly, slowly add the hot cream. Add soft butter, salt, and mix well. Reduce heat and simmer while stirring until it reaches 107°C (~225°F) (about 1 minute). Strain through a sieve and emulsify with an immersion blender. Cover with plastic wrap (touching the entire surface) and let cool
Combine all ingredients in a mixer bowl and whip until stable and the frosting texture leaves clear whisk marks

Once the cupcakes have cooled, use the back of a large piping tip to carve out a hole in the center. Fill each cupcake with 1 tsp of caramel and 1 tsp of peanut butter. Plug the hole with a small piece of cake, then pipe a swirl of cream on top using a closed star tip.

title: Choco-Caramel Cupcakes
steps: Preheat your oven to 160°C (~320°F) and line a muffin tin with large paper cupcake liners (60–70g batter per liner)
Boil 120g of water and allow it to cool slightly
In a large bowl, add all dry ingredients. Whisk until combined
In another bowl, add all wet ingredients, including the boiled water. Whisk until smooth
Gradually pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, stirring gently to combine. Make sure there are no lumps in the batter
Divide the batter evenly among the cupcake liners, fill them about 2/3 full. Bake for 20–25 min. Let the cupcakes cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely
In a saucepan, combine sugar, water, and glucose syrup. Place it over the heat to melt
Meanwhile, heat the cream to a boil in a separate saucepan
When the sugar syrup reaches a golden color (170–180°C or~338-356°F), carefully pour in the heated cream, stirring constantly
Add soft butter and salt, then stir well
Reduce heat and continue stirring while cooking until temp reaches 107°C (~225°F)(about 1 minute)
Strain the caramel through a sieve and blend with an immersion blender until smooth
Cover with plastic wrap (touching the surface) and allow to cool
Bring cream (1)to a boil and pour it over chopped dark chocolate. Let it sit for a minute, then stir until smooth
Add cream (2)and Baileys liqueur, combine well, cover with plastic wrap (touching the surface), and refrigerate overnight
Add mascarpone and whip with a mixer until the frosting is stable. Be careful not to overwhip the ganache
Once cooled, fill the cupcakes with caramel and decorate with chocolate Baileys frosting.

title: Pistachio-Tart Cherry Cupcakes
description: Salty hint of pistachio paired with refreshing tang of tart cherries By the way, I know that many of you have already tried my cupcake recipes. Leave a comment and let me know which flavor is your favorite

ingredients.name: unsalted butter (melt and cool to room temp, 82%)

steps: Preheat your oven to 175°C(~347°F) and line a muffin tin with paper cupcake liners
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, both sugars, baking powder, baking soda, and salt
In a separate bowl, combine melted butter, eggs, Greek yogurt, milk, and vanilla
Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Fold in chopped pistachios
Evenly distribute batter into cupcake liners, fill each about 2/3 full
Bake for 20–25 min, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
Let the cupcakes cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely
1vanilla bean
Place cherries in a saucepan. Mix cornstarch with lemon juice and water, then pour the mixture over the cherries. Stir and place over medium heat
In a separate bowl, mix sugar with pectin, then gradually add to the saucepan while stirring
Add vanilla bean and continue stirring until the mixture comes to a boil
Bring cream (1) to a boil and pour over chopped white chocolate (or callets) and pistachio paste. Add salt, let sit for a minute, then blend with an immersion blender until smooth
Add the cream (2) and combine with a spatula. Cover the surface with plastic food wrap and refrigerate overnight
Add mascarpone and whip with a mixer until the frosting is stable
Once cooled, fill the cupcakes with the cherry filling and decorate with the pistachio frosting.

title: HAZELNUT PRALINE RECIPE
description: I’m sharing my trusted recipe for vanilla praline with you — and if you’re saving it, be sure to thank me with a  and leave a comment! It’s quick to make, has a long shelf life, and tastes amazing in frostings, fillings, ganaches — or even just eaten by the spoonful!

ingredients.name: Fleur de Sel or ½ tsp regular salt

steps: Place hazelnuts and vanilla pods in the oven at 140°C (~285°F) for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine sugar, glucose syrup, and water in a saucepan and heat the syrup to 118°C (~244°F).
Once the syrup reaches this temperature, add vanilla pods and hot nuts, and begin caramelizing.
At a certain point, your syrup will completely crystallize. Don’t worry — that’s normal! Keep cooking until the sugar melts again and turns into a dry caramel.
Pour the caramelized hazelnuts onto a tray (ideally lined with a silicone mat or parchment paper), sprinkle with fleur de sel, and let cool.
Break into pieces and transfer to a blender or food processor. Blend until it becomes a smooth paste.
Yield: ~380 g of praline.
By the way, you can substitute almonds or peanuts for hazelnuts.

title: CHOCOLATE ORANGE CUPCAKES
description: Delicate cupcakes that combine the rich bitterness of chocolate with the explosive citrusy freshness of juicy oranges. Save the recipe, leave a like , and share your thoughts in the comments—your support inspires me to keep sharing!
steps: Mix the softened butter with the sugar until light and fluffy.
Sift the dry ingredients together and mix until combined.
Add half of the eggs to the butter mixture and mix. Add 1/3 of the dry ingredients, mix.
Add the remaining eggs and mix until incorporated. Add another third of the dry ingredients, mix.
Add the sour cream, orange zest, and liqueur, and mix until smooth. Finally, add the last third of the dry ingredients.
Spoon the batter into cupcake molds, filling each about 1/3 full.
Bake in a preheated oven at 170–180°C for 20–25 min.
Place all the ingredients into a saucepan, bring to a boil, then remove from heat and let cool.
- I used an orange compote for the filling (recipe in the previous post).
- You can also add caramel if desired.
- If you’d like an easy, fail-proof recipe for perfect caramel, let me know in the comments.
Chop the chocolate and melt it in the microwave in short bursts. Allow it to cool to r.temp.
Add the softened butter to melted chocolate and mix on low speed until combined.
Add the r.temp. cream cheese and mix again until smooth.
Lastly, incorporate the liqueur and orange zest.
Transfer the frosting into a piping bag and let it rest until it is still soft but holds its shape well.
Soak the cupcakes with the syrup, fill them with the compote, and decorate with the frosting, orange zest, and small pieces of orange.

title: PERFECT ORANGE COMPOTE RECIPE
description: This filling turns out incredibly fragrant and delicious — the rich citrus flavor of orange is perfectly complemented by the exotic tang of passion fruit. If you’re saving the recipe, please leave a comment below — it would make me very delighted!
steps: Pour the passion fruit purée into a saucepan and add the orange pulp (1). Place over medium heat.
Mix the sugar thoroughly with the pectin, then gradually sprinkle it into the saucepan while stirring constantly. Add the orange zest.
Bloom the gelatin by soaking it in cold water.
Bring the fruit mixture to a boil, then remove from the heat. Add the gelatin and stir until it is fully dissolved.
Add the remaining orange pulp (2). Cover the entire surface of the compote directly with plastic food wrap and chill until it has stabilized.
Optional: You can add a used vanilla bean pod or 20–25 g of the candied orange peel from the previous recipe.
This filling is perfect for sponge cakes, mousse cakes, macarons, choux pastries, and more.

title: TART CHERRY COCONUT CUPCAKE RECIPE
description: One of my all-time favorite combinations: crunchy coconut flakes paired with the refreshing tartness of tart cherries, all beautifully balanced by the gentle sweetness of white chocolate. Save this recipe so you don’t lose it. Thank you for your support —now let’s bake and enjoy
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a cupcake tin with paper liners.
Combine the dry ingredients in a stand mixer bowl. Add the butter and mix until the texture resembles fine crumbs.
Add the wet ingredients and mix thoroughly until smooth.
Portion evenly into the cupcake liners, sprinkle with coconut flakes, and bake for ~20 minutes.
Place the cherries in a small saucepan. Mix the cornstarch with the lemon juice and/or water, and add to the cherries. Stir and place over medium heat.
Combine the sugar and pectin, then slowly incorporate them into the mixture while stirring.
Add the vanilla pod and bring to a boil, stirring constantly.

title: GANACHE:
steps: Bring the first portion of cream (1) to a boil and pour over the chopped chocolate. Let  it sit for a minute, then stir until smooth.
Add the second portion of cream (2) and the coconut liqueur. Mix until combined, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight.
Once chilled, add the mascarpone and coconut flakes and whip until smooth and airy.

title: DECADENT CHOCOLATE BROWNIE RECIPE
description: - There’s nothing quite like cozying up on a brisk fall evening with a rich, indulgent chocolate brownie and a warm cup of cocoa. Save this recipe, thank me by the post, and grab your ingredients to get started!
steps: Melt the butter and dark chocolate separately in microwave-safe bowls. Combine and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs with the white and brown sugars, salt, and vanilla extract until well-blended.
Add the melted chocolate mixture to the eggs.

Sift in the flour and cocoa powder together, then gently fold in the batter until incorporated. Fold the nuts and chocolate chips in if desired. Alternatively, sprinkle them over the batter once it has been poured into the pan.
Pour the batter into a 20x30 cm baking pan lined with parchment paper and bake at 180°C (~355°F) for approximately 30 minutes.
Allow the brownies to cool, then cut into squares. Enjoy!
P.S. No brown sugar? Simply substitute with an equal amount of white sugar.

title: HAZELNUT SHORTBREAD PASTRY
description: Continuing to share the shortbread recipes! Today, we’re making a sweet shortbread pastry with hazelnut flour—perfect for nut tarts, cookies, and chocolate desserts. Be sure to save the recipe and this post!
steps: In a mixer bowl, combine the butter, powdered sugar, salt, egg, and vanilla at low speed until well-blended.
Add the all-purpose flour and hazelnut flour, mixing until the dough becomes smooth.
Transfer the dough to parchment paper or plastic wrap; roll it out as thinly as possible for quicker chilling.
Cover and refrigerate.
- Hazelnut flour can be substituted with any other nut flour, such as almond or pistachio.

title: RECIPE FOR TIRAMISU CUPCAKES
description: Even if traditional Italian tiramisu isn’t your favorite, these cupcakes are sure to win you over! Moist, espresso-soaked cupcakes paired with a delicate mascarpone cream create the perfect harmony of flavors that will capture your heart. - This simple recipe is always within reach! Enjoy, and don’t forget to leave a and save this post so you can easily find it later! INGREDIENTS (for 12 cupcakes):

ingredients.name: instant coffee, and cocoa for dusting

steps: · A shot of espresso for soaking
Preheat your oven to 160°C (~320°F) and line a 12-count muffin pan with paper liners.
Combine the dry ingredients. In a separate bowl, cream the butter and sugar together, then gradually add room-temperature eggs.
Slowly incorporate the dry ingredients, followed by the sour cream, oil, and vanilla. Divide the batter in half.
Mix instant coffee into one half of the batter. Alternate spooning both batters into the cupcake molds, swirling with a toothpick for a marbled effect.
Bake for 20-23 minutes, then allow the cupcakes to cool.
To prepare the frosting, whip all the ingredients together until smooth. Drizzle each cupcake with 1-2 teaspoons of espresso, frost with the mascarpone cream, and finish with a dusting of cocoa.

title: PÂTE BRISÉE RECIPE
description: Continuing to share more delicious shortbread dough recipes! Today, I’m sharing a classic pâte brisée—perfect for pies, tarts, and quiches. Save this recipe, and don’t forget to tap on the post!
steps: Sift the flour, salt, and sugar into a mixing bowl with a round bottom.
Cut the cold butter into cubes. Rub it into the flour until the mixture resembles fine crumbs. Create a well in the center.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, water, and vanilla. Pour into the well and mix until a soft dough forms.
Wrap the dough in plastic food wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes before use.

title: RECIPE FOR “VANILLA PANA-COTTA” CHEESECAKE
description: An incredibly tender dessert bursting with vanilla flavor while it melts in your mouth! A crunchy base with crushed nuts and desiccated coconut combined with a delicate creamy cheesecake layer creates a unique taste that will be remembered for a long time.

ingredients.name: basic crumb (recipe you can find in my stories, also will be pinned later in the highlights)

steps: - Slightly toast the nuts until golden brown, then let it cool and finely chop.
- Grind in pulses the crumb into fine crumbs in a food processor.
- Mix the crumbs with the nuts and desiccated coconut. Add softened butter and coconut oil and combine until homogeneous.

- Line the bottom of a cake form (mine is 20*30 cm) tightly with foil. Form the cheesecake base by pressing the shortcrust crumbs firmly onto the bottom. Place the cheesecake crust in a freezer for at least 30 minutes.
- Beat cream cheese, cornstarch, and sugar in a mixer bowl with a paddle attachment until creamy.
- Gradually add eggs and mix well. Add heavy cream, vanilla paste, and lemon juice, and mix until smooth.
- Pour the cheese mixture into the prepared cheesecake crust and bake at 120-130°C for about 90-120 minutes — the finished cheesecake should jiggle slightly in the middle, like a pudding.
- Let it cool and refrigerate overnight for stabilization.
- Soak gelatin in cold water and let it sit and bloom.
- In a saucepan, pour 130 g heavy cream with sugar and bring to boil. Add gelatin, stir until completely dissolved.
- Add the rest of heavy cream, vanilla seeds, mix, and pour over the cheesecake. Place in the fridge for 2 hours to set.
To remove the finished dessert from a cake form, warm it with a hairdryer from all sides. Cut the cheesecake into portions with a warm knife.

title: BASIC SAVORY CRUMBLE RECIPE FOR CHEESECAKE CRUST
description: I vividly recall your persistent request to add savory flavors into our second online course on cheesecakes! Intrigued by the idea, I embarked on the delightful journey of creating impeccable savory cheesecakes. A key challenge was to transform the sweet crumble into a savory counterpart. After a bit of experimentation, I successfully achieved the desired outcome, and I’m excited to generously share the recipe with you today
steps: - Combine softened butter and icing sugar until well mixed. Add the egg melange and mix again. Incorporate sifted flour and cornstarch, ground nuts, and salt. Mix everything with a mixer for 30–40 seconds until crumbly. Be cautious not to overmix the dough.

- Transfer the shortcrust crumbs onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, spread them evenly, and place in the freezer for at least 30 minutes. Bake in a preheated oven at 170–180 °C for approximately 15–20 minutes. Allow the crumble to cool completely. The baked shortcrust crumble should be crisp and golden.
The basic savory crumble is now ready!

- to form the cheesecake crust with savory crumble, I typically incorporate some ground nuts, spices to taste, around 20–30 g of milk, 20 g of butter, and 15 g of coconut oil into the baked shortcrust crumble
Swipe through the carousel and enjoy enticing photos of savory cheesecakes — Philadelphia, Marseille, and, of course, Crepes with Red Caviar

title: AUTHENTIC NAMELAKA RECIPE FROM VALRHONA SCHOOL RESEARCH KITCHENS
description: I know you’ve been eagerly awaiting the recipe, and here it is. To prepare the namelaka, you will need:
steps: - an emulsion blender
- a heat-resistant silicone spatula, a bowl, and a saucepan
▪ While stirring, melt the chocolate over a water bath or in short pulses in the microwave.
▪ Soak the gelatin in cold water and allow it to swell.
▪ In a saucepan, bring the milk to a boil, then add the glucose syrup and the squeezed gelatin.
▪ Carefully pour 1/3 of the boiling mixture into the melted chocolate in a thin stream, stirring intensively with a spatula until a homogeneous and glossy mass forms.
▪ Repeat the previous step two more times, incorporating the second portion of the boiling mixture into the chocolate, and then the remaining third portion.
▪ Pour in the cold heavy cream and process the mixture with a blender until it’s smooth.
▪ Cover the namelaka with cling film, ensuring it touches the surface of the namelaka, and place it in the fridge to stabilize for at least 12 hours.
This is the original recipe.
Now, in advance of any questions you may have:

- Use chocolate and gelatin according to the percentage of cocoa. Instead of dark chocolate, for example, you can use 350 g of milk chocolate 40% + 5 g of gelatin or 340 g of white chocolate 34% + 4 g of gelatin.
- Leaf gelatin can be replaced with powdered gelatin by converting between different strengths of gelatin.
- Glucose syrup is added to give the namelaka a silky texture and extend its shelf life. If you prefer, you can replace it with honey or omit it altogether.
- If you don’t have an emulsion blender, use a regular hand blender, making an effort to avoid incorporating any air bubbles, or mix the mixture until it’s smooth using a silicone spatula.

title: RECIPE FOR ALMOND TEA CAKE WITH ALMOND STREUSEL
description: #marusya_recipe UA Ukrainian version @ma_rusya_manko - moist, tender and incredibly delicious - with the captivating flavors of coffee and almond - topped with a satisfyingly crunchy streusel layer Ever since I first made Gordon Ramsay’s almond tea cake, inspired by the alluring image shared by @inn5775, the recipe has firmly nestled itself as one of my cherished autumn favorites. Make sure to delight your loved ones with this tea cake on a brisk September day. And please, take a moment to show your appreciation with a like and comment, acknowledging the dedication of my team and me. - for this recipe, you’ll need two 21x11 cm rectangular molds, h = 11 cm
steps: - Grind the almonds into small pieces using a food processor or blender.
- Quickly rub ground nuts, flour, sugar, and cold butter with your hands until crumbs form. Place in the fridge for at least 20–30 minutes.
- to make streusel crumbs, make sure to use butter that has been well-chilled in the fridge or slightly frozen in the freezer
- Grind the almonds into small pieces using a food processor or blender.

- Place soft butter in a mixer bowl, add sugar. Using a paddle attachment, beat at high speed until you get a light, fluffy mass. Then, add the eggs one at a time, thoroughly mixing the mass each time until it becomes smooth.

- Pour in the almond extract, add ground almonds, and combine thoroughly. Sift the flour, and mix it with baking powder and salt using a whisk. Pour in coffee (1), add dry ingredients, and mix until the batter is smooth. Pour in the remaining coffee (2) and mix thoroughly again.
- if desired, almond extract can be replaced with Amaretto liqueur or other almond liqueur to taste, or omitted altogether.

title: RECIPE FOR SOUR CHERRY CONFIT CHEESECAKE
description: The luscious sour cherry confit gracefully flowing off the tender, succulent cheese center, awakens the cravings of even the most ardent sweet tooth. And when the eye catches a crispy chocolate crust, a dessert fork mysteriously materializes in your hand, as if by magic! Savoring this wonderfully uncomplicated yet delicious cheesecake, you’ll find yourself in a state of pure gastronomic bliss. Remember my promise of a chic recipe? Well, here it is! #marusya_recipe
steps: - Mix soft butter (1) and icing sugar until combined. Add the egg yolk and mix again. Add flour, sifted together with cocoa powder, salt and mix everything for 20–30 seconds until crumbs have formed.

- Put the shortcrust crumbs on a baking sheet lined with a piece of parchment paper, distribute them evenly and put in the freezer for at least 30 minutes. Bake in the oven, preheated to 170–180 °C, for about 15–18 minutes.

- I advise you to bake the crumbs in 2 stages. First, bake the crumble for about 8–10 minutes at a higher temperature (180 °C). Then, take the baking sheet out of the oven and, using a metal dough scraper, mix and lightly chop the crumble. Finally, place the baking sheet in the oven for another 8–10 minutes at a lower temperature (160–170 °C) to ensure even browning and drying
- Allow the baked crumble to cool down completely and then grind it in pulses into fine crumbs in a food processor or blender. Add soft butter (2) and milk, and mix thoroughly.

title: COTTAGE CHEESE AND BERRY CRUMBLE PIE RECIPE
description: Greetings everyone! Did you get a chance to explore our latest cupcake recipe set? I hope you managed to purchase it with a super promotional deal and thereby help us raise funds to support the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Today I’d like to share with you a recipe for a scrumptiously delightful pie from my cookbook. #marusya_recipe
steps: - Cottage cheese and berry filling
▪ bilberries or blueberries
- Sift flour, mix it with baking powder and salt using a whisk. Pour the mixture into the mixer bowl, and add the butter, grated with a coarse grater.
- before grating the butter, place it in the freezer for half an hour

- In another bowl, whisk together sugar and egg yolks until a fluffy and light mixture forms. Transfer the egg-sugar mixture into the mixing bowl and mix the dough using a paddle attachment. Start at low speed, gradually progressing to medium speed, until the dough comes together into a single mass that detaches from the sides of the mixer bowl.

- Divide the finished dough into 2 pieces (one should be slightly larger than the other), and wrap each piece tightly with cling film. Put the larger piece of dough in the fridge, and place the smaller piece in the freezer for at least 2–3 hours, preferably overnight.
- Pass the cottage cheese through a sieve. Add sour cream, egg yolks, vanilla and caster sugar, rub the mixture with your hands. Add semolina and cornstarch, then mix thoroughly until smooth.
- to make the pie lighter, you can swap out sour cream for low-fat yogurt. Conversely, if you seek a richer pie, substitute the sour cream with butter

title: RECIPE FOR THE APRICOT ROULADE
description: The history of the recipe creation traces back to a scorching day in July, when I came across delectable apricots gracing the market counter. Allured by their enticing price and succulent flesh, I ended up buying a considerable quantity. The amount of apricots was so significant that it inspired me to make a delightful apricot jam, which you can see in the cross section of this heavenly roulade. With the cream cheese frosting, lavishly applied on the surface, the dessert achieved a well-rounded taste, which noticeably hastened the disappearance of its portions from the dessert plates Ready your apricots, because here comes the recipe! #marusya_recipe
steps: - Separate the eggs into yolks and whites. Combine 50 g of sugar and salt with the egg yolks, and whip until the mixture reaches its maximum volume. In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites with 70 g of sugar until they form medium peaks. Gradually add the sugar in 2–3 portions after the egg foam has formed.
- Gently fold the meringue into the whipped egg yolks. Mix the flour with the baking powder, sift and gradually incorporate into the egg mixture.
- Combine the milk and vegetable oil, add a portion of the batter into the milk-oil mixture, mix well until smooth. Pour this mixture back into the main batter, mix thoroughly.
- The temperature of the sponge batter should not exceed 18 °C, otherwise the batter will thicken and become less airy
- Bake the sponge on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper in an oven, preheated to 170 °C, for about 25–30 minutes.

title: RECIPE FOR THE APRICOT HONEY CAKE
description: The cake features a light, snow-white cloud of frosting adorned with sunny apricot halves, perfectly capturing its essence. Fragrant honey cake layers delicately covered by a layer of airy sour cream frosting and explosive apricot coulis create a harmonious balance, akin to a gentle breeze on a warm July day. With apricot season in full swing, let’s grab the recipe and find culinary zen in our kitchens #marusya_recipe
steps: - Frosting for coating

- Lightly whisk the eggs with sugar in a thick-bottomed saucepan, add honey, butter and place the saucepan over low heat. Stirring constantly, boil the mixture until sugar crystals are completely dissolved.

- Remove from the heat, add baking soda, and mix thoroughly. The mass should foam well and increase in volume. Pour the mixture into a separate bowl and add 500 g of sifted flour, mix with a spoon until smooth. Set aside for 10–15 minutes.
- if the dough remains excessively sticky after 10–15 minutes, sift the remaining 50 g of flour and add only as much as the dough can absorb.

- Divide the dough into 9 equal pieces (~105 g each) and form dough balls. Roll out each dough ball on a piece of parchment paper into a thin layer ~ 26 cm in diameter, prick with a fork and bake in the oven for about 3–5 minutes at 180 °C.

- Using a cake ring and a small knife, cut out 24-cm diameter circles from the still warm cake layers. Allow them to cool completely. Grind the scraps into fine crumbs using a food processor or coffee grinder, and use them to decorate the cake.

title: RECIPE FOR CHOCOLATE HONEYCOMB
description: All honey cakes that you see in the carousel are very symbolically garnished with shiny chocolate decorations in the form of honeycombs Honestly, it's hard to even count how many times our chef was asked to share the recipe for these cuties. Over time, a paid PDF recipe will appear on our website, but today we are sharing it with you completely free of charge, revealing all the tips and tricks. If you like it, support us with a like and comment - This variation of the recipe is the most intricate, as the chocolate decorations are colored in cold or pastel shades. #marusya_recipe You will need:
steps: - Silikomart Miel 8 silicone mold

▪ Moisten a small piece of cheesecloth with ethyl alcohol or any other alcohol-containing solution and carefully rub the silicone mold to a glossy shine. This will help you clean the mold and get a product with a perfect shiny surface.
- To prevent small particles from the cut ends of the cheesecloth from getting on the surface of the mold, fold the cheesecloth with the cut side facing inward
▪Place 100 g of white chocolate (1) in a plastic bowl and melt it in pulses in the microwave until it reaches ~40–45 °C.
- To melt the chocolate, use a low microwave power setting and heat it in short intervals. After each pulse, make sure to stir vigorously with a spatula.
▪Add 1–2 tsp. sifted titanium dioxide to melted chocolate and carefully mix with a silicone spatula until it completely dissolves.
- Titanium dioxide is used only to obtain cold or pastel shades. If your chocolate will be colored in warm colors or not colored at all, just skip this step.

▪Add ~20 g of white chocolate callets (2) while stirring vigorously. Wait until it has completely dissolved and check the temperature. If it hasn’t reached the required ~34–35 °C, repeat the procedure with fewer callets. Add 2–3 drops of color, and mix thoroughly until a uniform color is obtained.

title: RECIPE FOR THE SOUR CREAM CAKE
description: Today we’d like to share with you a recipe for a classic, easy-to-make cake with a pleasant sourness of delicate sour cream cake layers and airy sour cream frosting. The addition of poppy seeds, raisins and walnuts makes the texture and taste of each cake layer unique, while real vanilla seeds add noble spicy notes to the traditional frosting. The thinnest layer of chocolate icing slowly melting on the tongue perfects the flavor composition with its pleasant chocolate bitterness. Read the recipe, save the post and don’t forget to thank the chef with a like and a comment #marusya_recipe

ingredients.name: vanilla pod or 25 g vanilla paste

steps: - Pour 1 egg into the mixer bowl, add 75 g sugar and 5 g vanilla powder, whip on medium speed, increasing it to maximum, until a light and fluffy mass is formed. Add 150 g sour cream and whip again for a few minutes on maximum speed.
- Sift the flour and mix it with baking powder. Reduce the mixer speed to minimum and add the dry ingredients in 2–3 lots. Add finely chopped nuts and mix again thoroughly.

- Transfer the dough to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and form a rectangle (around 34 x 17 cm) by evenly distributing the dough with slightly moistened hands over the entire surface of the baking sheet. Bake in the oven for about 15–20 minutes at 180 °C until the top browns lightly.

- Carefully remove the baked cake layer from the baking sheet using two large offset spatulas or long knives, let it cool down completely, then carefully peel off the parchment paper and cut out a 32 x 15 cm rectangle using a ruler and a knife.

title: RECIPE FOR STRAWBERRY MOJITO ZEPHYR
description: UA Ukrainian version @ma_rusya_manko The bright, rich, refreshing and unforgettable taste of this zephyr won’t leave you indifferent on these warm summerlike days! The first reaction of all who tasted it: - Does it contain alcohol?! - There’s not a single drop of alcohol in the composition! How is this possible? Study the recipe, prepare the zephyr and have a bite! Let's go! #marusya_recipe
steps: - Wash firm, green sour apples thoroughly. Cut them into quarters and remove the core. Leave the skin on as it contains the most pectin.
- The most suitable varieties are Granny Smith, Simirenko and Antonovka
- Cover a baking sheet with parchment paper, arrange apples on it and place them in the oven, preheated to 170–180 °C, for 30–60 minutes (depending on the amount of apples).

- Put baked apples, lime pulp, cut into small pieces, and strawberries in a saucepan, add 100 g of sugar (1) and place over low heat. Once the sugar has completely dissolved, reduce the heat to medium and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring constantly. Let the mixture simmer for 5–8 minutes over low heat until softened.

- Process the hot mixture with a hand blender until smooth and pass it through a sieve. Pour the puree back into the saucepan and place it over low heat. Stirring constantly, sprinkle in 50 g of sugar (2) premixed with 6–7 g of pectin. Bring to a boil and let it simmer for about 5–7 minutes. Cool the finished jam to 30–35 °C.

title: RECIPE FOR QUICHE WITH SALMON AND GORGONZOLA
description: The smell of baked salmon in a creamy egg sauce with pieces of gorgonzola and broccoli drives my family members crazy! They don't give the quiche a second to cool! Check out the recipe, bookmark it and treat your loved ones to a new, savory pastry! I wonder if your quiche will have time to cool #marusya_recipe
steps: - Put the whole grain and all-purpose flour (both sifted) in the mixer bowl, add the cold diced butter and mix with a flex edge paddle attachment until crumbs form.
- if a flex edge paddle attachment is not available, you can chop the dough with a knife until fine crumbs form
- Add egg yolks, water, salt and mix until the dough comes together. Immediately after this, stop the mixer. Slightly roll the dough out, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 1–2 hours.

- if desired, you can make a bit bigger batch of the shortcrust pastry to seal cracks that may form at the joints of the dough during baking; if such cracks have formed in your crust, be sure to seal them to prevent the leakage of the sauce

- Roll out the dough into a round layer (23–25 cm in diameter and 3–4 mm thick). Using a rolling pin, carefully transfer the rolled out dough into the mold. Form the sides 4–5 cm high, prick the crust with a fork and put it in the freezer for 10–15 minutes.

- Take the mold from the freezer and line it with a sheet of parchment paper, place pie weights on top. Bake in the oven for about 15–18 minutes at 180 °C, then remove the weights and bake the crust for another 10 minutes until golden brown.
- pie weights keep the crust from puffing up or shrinking away from the edge of the mold — you can use small ceramic or metal balls, as well as beans, lentils or peas

title: RECIPE FOR BROWNIE BONBONS
description: Chocolate, an ingredient that pleases the ears with a nice crunch and has more than 1,500 flavor nuances, revealed its charismatic nature when creating these mega chocolate bonbons recipe for true chocoholics! It seems that it was not an angelic voice that prompted our chef to combine the alluring crispy crust and the brownie filling with the noble bitterness of dark chocolate ganache, slowly melting in the mouth. Can't wait to make these bonbons? Think twice — one certainly won't be enough #marusya_recipe
steps: - Melt the dark chocolate in pulses in the microwave. Separately, melt the butter and gently fold it into the chocolate. Allow the mixture to cool down slightly.
- Sift the flour with cocoa powder, add baking powder and mix thoroughly with a whisk.

- Beat the eggs together with the sugar until the mixture turns white and foamy. Pour the melted butter and chocolate into the egg mixture and stir until smooth. Introduce the dry ingredients, add salt and mix gently.

- Pour the finished batter into a cake ring (d = 24 cm) — make sure to cover the bottom of the ring tightly with foil and grease the sides with soft butter in advance). Bake in the oven, preheated to 170–180 °C, for about 15–20 minutes. Allow to cool down completely without removing the ring.

- Carefully peel off the foil, remove the brownie from the mold by running a knife along the sides of the ring, and wrap the brownie in cling film. Refrigerate for at least 4–6 hours to stabilize, preferably overnight.

title: HOMEMADE HAZELNUT PASTE
description: #marusya_theory_tips Today I will share with you some tips on how to easily and effortlessly make the hazelnut paste at home. The first and most important tip for getting an incredibly tasty and fragrant hazelnut paste is to use WELL-TOASTED nuts! - Got it? - Brilliant! To make the hazelnut paste you will need:
steps: - blender/food processor

- Arrange hazelnuts on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Toast them in the oven preheated to 150 °C for around 20-30 minutes until golden brown, stirring occasionally after the nuts begin to release oil — you should feel a pleasant nutty aroma. Remove skins if necessary.
- I recommend using well-toasted nuts only for making nut paste — for other purposes, such high toasting level is not appropriate, since hazelnuts become slightly bitter.
- Place the well-toasted nuts in the bowl of a blender or food processor and process until they begin to actively release oil and acquire a pasty consistency.
- to get a uniform texture of the paste, use at least 200 g of toasted nuts (depending on the diameter of your blender bowl)
- in the process of grinding, don’t forget to stop the blender and mix the paste with a spatula occasionally, scraping it from the walls of the bowl

- to speed up the blending process, you can add a little odorless vegetable oil, but I usually don’t do this — firstly, the hazelnuts start to release oil during grinding, and secondly, extra oil makes the nut paste runny and, as a result, affects the texture of frosting or ganache made with the addition of nut paste
That's it — the hazelnut paste is ready!
Use the finished nut paste for making various types of fillings and ganaches — it will give them an unforgettable rich nutty flavor!

steps: - Melt the sugar in a thick-bottomed saucepan (do not stir it). While sugar is melting, heat up honey and butter.
- Remove the saucepan from the heat and pour hot honey into the melted sugar, mix. Then add the melted hot butter and mix well again. Let the mixture cool down to ~70 °C.

- Incorporate a third of the flour and all the eggs into the caramel mixture, mix until smooth and add baking soda and citric acid. Mix vigorously until the mixture has foamed well. Add the rest of the flour and mix with a tablespoon until well incorporated. Let the dough cool down for about 15 minutes.

- Divide the dough into 5 equal pieces. Roll out each piece on parchment paper into a thin layer 2-3 mm thick, then cut out an even rectangle ~24x34 cm. Roll out a thin layer from the scraps of dough, which will later be needed for making crumbs.
- Prick the layers with a fork and bake in a preheated oven at 170 °C for 4-6 minutes until golden brown. While the cake layers are still hot, trim off the edges to get rectangles measuring 20x30 cm.

steps: For the dough:

Making the preferment:

title: RAFFAELLO’ ZEPHYR RECIPE
description: by @marusya.manko Russian version @ma_rusya_manko #ma_rusya_recipe

ingredients.name: glucose or glucose and fructose syrup

steps: - Place the baked apples into a saucepan, add a couple of tbsp. of water, 100 g of sugar and put it over low heat. When the sugar has completely dissolved, switch the heat to medium and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally. Let it simmer for about 2-3 minutes.
- Process the hot mixture with a blender until completely homogeneous and pass it through a sieve if desired.

- Place the puree over low heat and, stirring constantly, gradually sprinkle in 50 g of sugar mixed with 7 g of pectin. Bring the mixture to a boil and keep it boiling constantly mixing for about 7-8 minutes.
- Cool the puree down to 30-35 °C.
- ‘Raffaello’ zephyr
- Pour the jam into a mixer bowl, add 7-8 g of albumin, mix thoroughly and set it aside for 15 minutes, then put whipping at slow speed.
- instead of albumin, you can use 45-50 g of raw egg white. In the latter case, I advise you to cook the jam longer and let it stabilize overnight in the refrigerator.
- Pour 100 g of water, 50 g of rum and coconut water into a saucepan and add agar-agar.
- if rum and/or coconut water is not available, use the same amount of water instead
- Place the saucepan over medium heat and, stirring constantly, bring the mixture to a boil. Then add sugar and glucose or glucose and fructose syrup, mix. Increase the mixer speed.
- Keep stirring and bring the syrup to a boil. Cook until 108-110C. The finished syrup should run off the spatula in a continuous stream.

title: QUICHE LORRAINE RECIPE
description: with salmon, broccoli and gorgonzola Russian version @ma_rusya_manko I saw the recipe for this delicious pastry at Mary’s account @mary.s_kitchen_. steps: - Mix the dry ingredients. Add the cold diced butter and turn everything into a crumble with a mixer (with a paddle attachment) or chop it with a knife.
- Add the yolk, water and salt. As soon as the dough can be shaped into a ball, stop mixing it. Slightly roll out the dough, wrap it in plastic wrap and put in the fridge for 1-2 h.
- Roll out the dough into a layer 3-4 mm thick and put it in a mold d=18 cm, making the borders 4-5 cm high, prick with a fork and put it in the freezer for 10-15 min.
- Put a sheet of parchment paper on top of the dough in the mold and fill it with some weight (e.g. beans or lentils).
- Bake it in a preheated oven for 15 min with the weight on and 10 min without it, until the base is lightly browned.
- Dice the salmon, removing the pin bones. Crumble the cheese with your hands into small pieces.
- Disassemble the broccoli into separate inflorescences, cut large ones into pieces and cook them for 1-2 min in boiling salted water. Pour into a colander to drain.
Egg and sour cream mixture:
salt, pepper to taste *
- Mix all ingredients until homogeneous.
- Put the filling into the base, pour the egg and sour cream mixture on top. Bake at 200°C/392°F for about 40-50 min. The filling should set.
- Let the quiche cool down for 20 min.
* Be sure to taste your cheese before adding salt to the egg and sour cream mixture. If it's too salty, then don’t add salt to it.

title: SAN SEBASTIAN BASQUE BURNT CHEESECAKE RECIPE
description: Judging by your reaction to my stories I understood that not everyone has heard of this Spanish variation of a cheesecake, and, what is more, not everyone has tried it. Your messages like "Can't you see that it burned down?!" clearly proved it. Those who didn't ask me such questions, probably thought the same, right? I was enchanted by the simplicity of this recipe! A child's play – you put all the ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth, then pour into a mold and "burn" in the oven at maximum temperature. But ... I had to remake it at least a dozen times till I finally achieved the desired result. As you can see, there were also some fine details and nuances. The first cheesecake turned out to be like a curd cheese casserole, same thing happened to the second one. I changed the recipe. It turned out better, but still not perfect. I tediously had been choosing the baking mode, as well as the size of the cake ring. In short, the whole point of this cheesecake is that it should be burnt on top, while remaining slightly underbaked on the inside. Two worst pastry chef's nightmares legally settled in this recipe – a burnt crust and an underbaked centre. Many of you DM me to buy the recipe, but I promised that I would publish the recipe for free. If I had known how much effort it would require, I would have reconsidered promising that. Just kidding. As you can see, the recipe is hard-won and torn from my heart. I hope you appreciate it and shower me with
steps: - Preheat oven to 230 °C / 446 °F with upper and lower heat mode on. Line an 18 cm cake ring with two parchment paper sheets.
- Put all the ingredients into a blender and process until smooth. Pour the mixture into the prepared mold.
- Bake the cheesecake until its top is burnt. In my oven it takes about 30 minutes. The ready cheesecake should jiggle very well in the center.
- Let the cheesecake cool down, then put it in the fridge overnight.
